language.script_notes: Bengali script hangs its letters from a horizontal line and is also used in the Indian state of West Bengal, so the script alone does not separate the two — it does rule out Devanagari-script India and most of South Asia. English appears widely as a second language on signs.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Red-and-white striped bollards, chimney-shaped and painted in alternating sections; also on fences beside water.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Chimney-shaped concrete posts, often clustered near bridges.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Minimal on most roads; low painted barriers near bridges.
road_furniture.line_paint: Yellow and white markings where roads are marked; many roads have none.
road_furniture.curb_style: Mostly absent; roads are crowded to the edge with stalls, rickshaws and pedestrians.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Many road signs sit on black-and-white striped poles (also seen in Bhutan), and utility poles are often wooden or concrete. Red-and-white bollards cluster near bridges.

architecture.roof_style: Pitched roofs — gabled (dochala) or hipped (chochola) — on rural houses, with flat concrete roofs on urban buildings.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated tin sheet is the most popular roofing, used widely by rural families; thatch on more traditional houses.
architecture.wall_construction: Rural houses of mud, bamboo, timber and tin on a raised earth plinth, usually single-storey around an open courtyard; kiln-fired brick and cement in towns; ornate brick and terracotta mosques and old zamindar mansions in historic areas.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Earthy brown mud and grey tin in the countryside; bare brick and weathered concrete in cities.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Tin-roofed village houses; brick kilns with tall chimneys dotting the plains; Dhaka's extremely dense high-rise and low-rise mix; mosques with domes and minarets; ship-breaking yards on the Chittagong coast.

nature.vegetation: Flat, waterlogged rice paddies stretch to the horizon; dense village groves of banana, palm, bamboo and mango; jute and vegetable fields; mangrove forest in the south.
nature.terrain: One of the flattest, most water-covered countries on Earth — a vast river delta of the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna, with monsoon flooding, small hills only in the far southeast (Chittagong Hill Tracts) and northeast.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid and hazy tropical monsoon; severe air pollution often limits visibility in the distance.

vehicles.plate_color: White plates for private vehicles and green plates for commercial ones (CNG three-wheelers and baby taxis), in contrast to India's yellow and white system.
vehicles.plate_format: City or district name in Bengali script followed by a class letter and digits.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Cycle rickshaws with colourful painted art and CNG auto-rickshaws ('baby taxis') swarm the roads; heavily decorated trucks and buses; Street View images often show red mirror reflections.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mixed official coverage with third-party imagery in places.
google_coverage.blur_style: Standard Google blurring, with red mirror reflections visible in the car imagery.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Concentrated on Dhaka, the Dhaka–Chittagong corridor and the main highways; more limited in rural areas.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same Bengali script, same delta landscape, similar rickshaws and rural houses
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Script does not separate them; green commercial plates, red-and-white chimney bollards and black-and-white striped sign poles point here, while India uses yellow commercial plates.

confusion_set.shared_traits: South Asian road culture; striped black-and-white sign poles shared with Bhutan
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Bengali script and the flat, water-covered delta separate it from mountainous Nepal and Bhutan.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared southeastern border hills and tropical vegetation
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Bengali versus Burmese script, and left-hand versus right-hand traffic (Myanmar drives on the right).
